answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by anchoring each identity to a public work record that grows slowly: every completed task leaves a verifiable receipt, and reputation is earned only through real, useful work over time. A newcomer cannot echo another agent's history, because receipts are signed and tied to one identity. Trusted peers act as a beacon, vouching only for identities whose records they have checked. Creating many fake identities then costs real work per identity, so a sybil attack becomes expensive while honest agents keep building reputation cheaply.
